storm.summary_layperson: No storms anywhere nearby tonight — high pressure is keeping skies clear and dry over Greenwich and the surrounding towns alike.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No marine-layer buffer: the Sound (63°F) is already warmer than the air (61°F) at 4 PM, and the gap only widens the other way as air cools to the mid-50s by 7 PM — the Sound isn't shaping the weather tonight.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: A strong high (pressure near 1027 hPa across the region) is in control. KOKX radar shows no echoes at all, there are no NWS alerts, and the atmosphere has no instability to work with (CAPE of 0 J/kg, wind shear only about 9 kt). The NWS forecast is simply “Sunny”.

Local effect: The cool-water “marine layer” that sometimes blunts summer storms needs the air to be at least ~5°F warmer than the Sound. Tonight it's the reverse: Bridgeport Harbor water is 63°F while the cove air is about 61°F, and the model cools the air to roughly 54°F by 7 PM. The Sound holds its temperature while the air cools after sunset, so the water only gets relatively warmer through the evening — no protective layer at any point in the window. There is no sea breeze running either. With no storms to modify, this doesn't matter today.

Cove vs. surrounding areas: Same as everywhere else in the region — dry, clear, cooling quickly after the 6:07 PM sunset.

What would change the call: Nothing in the current data points that way. A new radar echo or NWS alert would be needed to raise the risk, and the large-scale setup gives no sign of one tonight.

wind.regime_label: Light gradient wind — no sea breeze, direction wandering

hourly.shift_note: light and unsettled — cove showing SSE puffs
backing to NNE, offshore flow setting

wind.tactics_blurb: Light, wandering breeze that backs from ENE toward N through the evening — a persistent left shift, so favor the left side of the beat. Expect near-drifter conditions; keep the boat moving and hunt pressure in the middle of the cove.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
The call: light gradient wind, no sea breeze. The airports are only reporting around 7 kt on average, and the sea breeze never got going today — only 1 of 19 coastal stations shows a southerly, and the air–water temperature difference is negative (air 61°F vs. Sound 63°F, about −2°F). Without land warmer than water, there's no thermal engine, so the sea-breeze direction correction does not apply.

Direction through the window: The model (HRRR) has light east-northeast wind at 5 PM backing steadily to north-northeast by 7 PM as the land cools after the 6:07 PM sunset. Right now, though, the Riverside YC anemometer reads SSE at about 4 kt (10-min average), with gusts to 8 — nearly 90° off the model. Western Sound stations disagree widely too (direction agreement only 0.41), so treat the early part of the window as unsettled. Confidence in direction is low until the offshore flow sets in after sunset.

Where the pressure is: While the wind is east-ish, Greenwich Point shelters the cove heavily and the start line can be dead even when the open Sound has breeze. As it backs to NE the flow gets cleaner and more uniform, with slightly more pressure mid-cove. Once it goes N after dark, expect it to come off the land puffy and shifty, with holes between puffs — best average pressure in the middle of the cove, away from the trees on shore.

Shift character: This is a persistent backing trend (ENE → NNE → N), not an oscillating breeze — the wind keeps rotating left and doesn't come back. Favor the left side of upwind legs and don't bank on getting the right back.

What the fleet will feel: 4–5 kt, falling to around 3 kt by 10 PM. That's light-air, drifter-class sailing: heavier boats will struggle to hold way, and race committees may have trouble setting a square line with the direction moving this much. Chilly too — air drops into the mid-50s by 7 PM.

data_caveats: HRRR model data only available through 7 PM (forecast hours 5–12 failed to download) — 8–10 PM wind is extrapolated from the evening trend and is lower confidence.
